name: Title objection letter
what: The buyer's written objections to matters in the title commitment and survey, sent inside the contract's review period.

fields.label: Date sent
fields.definition: The date the letter was delivered, with the delivery method; compare both with the contract's notice clause.

fields.label: Objection deadline
fields.definition: The last day for objections under the contract, counted the way the contract counts days from delivery of the commitment, its documents and the survey.

fields.label: From
fields.definition: The buyer, and the counsel signing for it.

fields.label: To and copied
fields.definition: Each recipient the notice clause requires, and the title company and escrow agent copied.

fields.label: Commitment and survey reviewed
fields.definition: The title commitment objected to, by file number and effective date, and the survey by surveyor and date of the last revision.

fields.label: Objections
fields.definition: Each matter objected to: the Schedule B item, Schedule C requirement or survey finding by number, what it is, and how it affects the buyer's use, financing or value.

fields.label: Cure requested
fields.definition: For each objection, the cure the buyer asks for, such as a recorded release, a payoff at closing, deletion from the policy, an endorsement or a corrected survey.

fields.label: Matters accepted
fields.definition: Matters the letter accepts or does not object to, which the contract may treat as permitted exceptions.

fields.label: Endorsements requested
fields.definition: Title endorsements and policy amendments the buyer asks for, by form number, such as amendment of the area-and-boundary exception, access (T-23), contiguity (T-25) or restrictions, encroachments and minerals (T-19.1). The Texas Department of Insurance's list of promulgated title forms has no zoning endorsement.
fields.authority: Texas Department of Insurance, Title Insurance Basic Manual, Section II (Insuring Forms)

fields.label: Seller's response deadline
fields.definition: The date the seller must respond or cure under the contract, and what the contract says a silent seller is deemed to have chosen.

fields.label: Termination right
fields.definition: The buyer's right, as the letter states it, to terminate and recover the deposit if the seller does not cure, and the deadline to use it.

fields.label: Reservation for new matters
fields.definition: Any reservation of the right to object to matters that first appear in an updated commitment or survey.

fields.label: Seller's response
fields.definition: The seller's written answer to each objection, will cure, will not cure or cure in part, with the date it arrived.
